questions.prompt: Why does the DI setup start by removing `StartupUri="MainWindow.xaml"` from `App.xaml`?
options: Because `StartupUri` only works in .NET Framework WPF projects
So `App.xaml.cs` creates the window with an injected ViewModel
Because App.xaml may not contain any attributes once DI is used
So the app starts faster by skipping the XAML parsing step
questions.explanation: Removing `StartupUri` means WPF no longer creates the window for you, so `OnStartup` can build the container, create `MainWindow` with `DataContext = Services.GetRequiredService<MainViewModel>()` and show it.

questions.prompt: Put the steps of `OnStartup` in `App.xaml.cs`, used as the composition root, in order.
questions.explanation: The composition root registers services, builds the DI container, then creates the main window with an injected ViewModel and shows it.

source.section: Step 2 — Use App.xaml.cs as Composition Root

questions.prompt: Why does this lesson call `<Window.DataContext><vm:MainViewModel /></Window.DataContext>` a common mistake?
options: XAML cannot create objects from classes in your own namespaces
It creates two ViewModel instances for every window you open
It silently turns every binding in the window into OneTime
There is no constructor injection, so no DI and poor testability
questions.explanation: A ViewModel created in XAML gets no constructor injection, so it cannot receive services from DI and is hard to test. The composition root should resolve and inject it instead.

questions.prompt: In which shutdown scenario is `OnExit` **not** called?
options: The app crashes with an unhandled exception
The user clicks the window's close button
Code calls `Application.Shutdown()`
Windows shuts down while the app is open
questions.explanation: `OnExit` runs on normal close, `Application.Shutdown()` and Windows shutdown, but not on an unhandled crash, which is why logging and global exception handlers are critical.

questions.prompt: With the "prevent multiple instances" version of `WindowService.Show<TViewModel>()`, what happens when the user opens Settings while the Settings window is already open?
options: A second Settings window opens on top of the first one
`Show` throws an `InvalidOperationException` for the duplicate
The open window is found in `_openWindows` and activated
The existing window is closed and a fresh one is created
questions.explanation: `Show` checks `_openWindows.TryGetValue(type, out var existing)` and calls `existing.Activate()`; a window is only removed from the dictionary by its `Closed` handler.

source.section: Note : Prevent multiple instances of same window (common need)

questions.prompt: After `services.Configure<ApplicationSettings>(Configuration.GetSection("Application"))`, how does `MainViewModel` read the app name from `appsettings.json`?
options: It reads `App.Configuration["Application:Name"]` from the static property
It injects `IOptions<ApplicationSettings>` and reads `options.Value.Name`
It parses `appsettings.json` itself with `File.ReadAllText`
It is given the value through a XAML `StaticResource`
questions.explanation: The settings section is bound to a strongly typed POCO, and ViewModels receive it through `IOptions<T>` constructor injection, keeping them clean and testable.
